explanation: Magazine facts describe a separate entity, so they should be stored once in a `Magazine` table rather than repeated in every article row. Each article can then be related to its magazine, which matches the one-to-many structure and reduces redundancy.

options.text: Keep magazine details in a separate `Magazine` table and relate each article to its magazine
Store `article_id` in the `Magazine` table so each magazine points to one article
Copy magazine title, issue date, and editor into every article row
Use one table for both entities and leave magazine columns blank in many rows

prompt: A publisher stores magazines and articles. Each article belongs to exactly one magazine, but a magazine has many articles. The team also wants to prevent the same magazine facts from being copied into every article row. Which rule best fits this design?
reviewConcept: Separate repeated facts into their own entity in a one-to-many relationship.
